texts.secretariat_outline: Slavery and compulsory labour are inconsistent with the dignity of man and therefore prohibited by this Bill of Rights. But a man may be required to perform his just share of any public service that is equally incumbent upon all, and his right to a livelihood is conditioned by his duty to work. Involuntary servitude may also be imposed as part of a punishment pronounced by a court of law.
texts.cassin_draft: Slavery, which is inconsistent with the dignity of man, is prohibited. Public authority may impose a personal service or work only by application of a law and for the common interest.
texts.drafting_committee_1: Slavery, which is inconsistent with the dignity of man, is prohibited in all its forms.
texts.e_cn4_57: Slavery, in all its forms, being inconsistent with the dignity of man, shall be prohibited by law."
texts.geneva_draft: Slavery, in all its forms, being inconsistent with the dignity of man, shall be prohibited by law.
texts.drafting_committee_2: Slavery is prohibited in all its forms.
texts.chr_3: 1. No one shall be held in slavery or involuntary servitude. 2. No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
texts.a777: No one shall be held in slavery or servitude; slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.
texts.final: No one shall be held in slavery or servitude; slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.
